Sports.title: How Nottingham Forest will spend £116m Elliot Anderson warchest: The three Premier League midfielders being targeted, new striker on agenda and the latest on Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams' futures
Sports.content:
How Nottingham Forest will spend £116m Elliot Anderson warchest: The three Premier League midfielders being targeted, new striker on agenda and the latest on Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams' futures

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Forest camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The hard work starts here. Nottingham Forest have completed comfortably the biggest transfer deal in their history by selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for £116million, a record fee for an English player.

It is a stunning piece of business for Forest, who bought Anderson from Newcastle for £35m only two years ago. These deals will help Forest stay within spending rules and give them opportunity to replace Anderson while improving elsewhere.

Unlike last season, the club will not be involved in European competition and so probably do not need the sort of expensive recruitment drive they pursued a year ago. But Evangelos Marinakis remains one of the most ambitious owners in the Premier League and will expect a far better domestic season than last year, when Forest had four managers and were fighting relegation virtually to the end of the campaign.

Last summer Forest paid about £200m for 10 new players to handle the twin objectives of domestic and European football but of those, only Omari Hutchinson and Igor Jesus established themselves in the first team.

Never say never with Forest, who have form for recruiting heavily in the closing weeks of a summer window. Yet as things stand, and with no European football on the horizon, Forest are planning fewer signings – with a forward, a right back and at least one midfielder among the targets.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at how Forest will tackle the summer window.

Elliot Anderson will become the most expensive English player of all time when he completes his £116m move to Manchester City

Igor Jesus was one of the few new players to establish himself in the Nottingham Forest side last season

Who replaces Anderson?

Forest will be lucky to find another player on whom they can make such an enormous profit in a two-year period. But the club knew some time ago that Anderson would likely depart this summer and have begun assessing their options.

Brighton midfielder Jack Hinshelwood is a long-term target and Forest considered making an offer for him last winter. The player has since signed a new three-and-a-half-year deal on the south coast, but this remains one to keep an eye on, possibly until later in the window.

Forest are also thought to be considering Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones. Jones has one year remaining on his contract and it is thought the Reds will listen to offers for the 25-year-old, who is also of interest to Inter Milan. The Italian champions had a £21m bid rejected last week and it is thought Liverpool will not consider any offer below £35m.

The one issue is whether Jones, having been a useful but never a crucial player for his boyhood team, would be keen to join what he might deem a lower-ranked club. Some players like that also struggle to adapt when they are suddenly expected to be a key man for a new team.

Forest are also monitoring Swedish midfielder Lucas Bergvall, who is keen to leave Tottenham this summer due to a lack of first-team opportunities under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs beat Barcelona to sign the 20-year-old two years ago but he started only once in De Zerbi's seven matches at the end of last season.

He is currently at the World Cup, where he became Sweden's youngest player to appear in the competition. He supported Manchester United as a boy and had two trials with them, in 2020 and 2022.

Brighton midfielder Jack Hinshelwood is a long-term target and Forest considered making an offer for him last winter

Curtis Jones is also of interest, though Forest face competition from Italian champions Inter Milan

Lucas Bergvall is also on their radar after falling out of favour at Tottenham Hotspur

Will any other stars leave?

After Anderson, the three stars Forest fans were most concerned about losing were attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, full back Neco Williams and centre back Murillo.

Though Murillo has had interest from Manchester United and Chelsea, the Brazilian defender signed a new four-year contract last month and this should greatly improve Forest’s chances of hanging onto him this summer.

Gibbs-White is coming off the season of his life, producing 18 goals and seven assists in all competitions. However, this was not good enough to propel him into the England World Cup squad. As one of the best players in his position in the Premier League, Gibbs-White will always be of interest to wealthy rivals, but at this stage Forest are quietly confident he will stay.

First, Gibbs-White is comfortably the highest-paid player in Forest’s history, having signed a new three-year deal last summer days after Tottenham thought they had triggered a release clause in his previous contract.

Forest’s intention has always been to build their team around Gibbs-White and with Anderson gone, they are doubly determined to do so. They would also have to replace him – no easy job for a club like Forest, especially when there are few No 10s as good as Gibbs-White on the market.

Of course, Forest would have a decision to make in the event of a huge offer. Gibbs-White turns 27 in January and is in the prime of his career, so any bid would have to be well above Spurs’ £60m offer last summer even to be considered. Forest are relatively relaxed about the situation. They are not compelled to sell Gibbs-White and anyone trying to sign him would have a huge task convincing Marinakis to do business.

Williams also signed a new deal last summer but had another barnstorming campaign last year and is admired by many clubs across the league. Again, though, Forest know they would have a tough job replacing the Wales international, who can play in both full back positions and is rarely injured.

As we are not yet out of June, nothing can be ruled out. If Gibbs-White or Williams were to demand to leave, that may change the landscape – but Forest feel they are in a strong position.

Though Murillo has had interest from Manchester United and Chelsea, the Brazilian defender signed a new four-year contract last month

Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams both starred last season and Forest will try their hardest to keep them

Where else are they looking to strengthen and which fringe players could leave?

With Chris Wood now 34 and Jesus not considered a natural centre forward, Forest will prioritise signing a new striker this summer. There is also Taiwo Awoniyi, and Arnaud Kalimuendo will come back from his loan at Eintracht Frankfurt, but this will not prevent Forest from looking closely at a new goalscorer.

While much is expected of Jesus this season, coach Vitor Pereira believes he is stronger as a second striker or even a No 10 than as a No 9. Jesus adapted superbly to English football last season, scoring 16 goals in all, but admitted the difference in speed and physicality from the Brazilian top flight came as a shock. He should be even better this year.

Another area Forest are studying is right back. Ola Aina is a proven Premier League performer but he has struggled with injuries and Forest are keen to find a strong alternative, with Nicolo Savona available for transfer.

Others who could depart from the players signed last summer include Dilane Bakwa, Dan Ndoye and James McAtee, although Pereira is a huge admirer of McAtee. Offers may also be considered for back-up centre back Morato.

Forest need more firepower up front with Chris Wood now 34 and having had an injury-hit season

Dan Ndoye, who is currently at the World Cup with Switzerland, could leave this summer after failing to make a significant impact in his first season at Forest

How do Forest stand with financial rules?

Daily Mail Sport understands the club are in a good position for the 2025-26 Premier League accounting period, even before the sale of Anderson.

If the Anderson transfer is announced officially in July, it would then fall into the 2026-27 cycle and potentially give Forest more room for manoeuvre in the market.

UEFA have more stringent regulations, however, and Forest will soon learn whether they face a fine for exceeding the Squad Cost Ratio last season. This has happened before to Premier League clubs who compete in Europe after a long absence, with Wolves and Aston Villa being previous victims.

However, any UEFA punishment is unlikely to cloud the present picture, as Forest try to give Pereira a squad to ensure they do not face another relegation battle – or a four-manager season.

Sports.title: Newcastle add German World Cup star to their shortlist, the sell-on clause for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall revealed... and West Ham go in for Ghana star: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Koppen set for West Ham role

Nils Koppen is set to be appointed as director of player recruitment at West Ham.

Koppen, who is FC Copenhagen’s technical director, still needs to obtain a work permit, but the intention is he will lead the recruitment of players though will not be responsible for the overall football operation.

The Belgian was formerly with Rangers and PSV Eindhoven.

Newcastle’s Steve Nickson was also linked with West Ham but, as Daily Mail Sport revealed, he is a candidate for a role with Wrexham.

Hammers in for Fatawu

West Ham have registered their interest in Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with the Championship side preparing for life without Crysencio Summerville.

Fatawu is with Ghana at the World Cup while Summerville is with the Netherlands squad and is attracting interest from Manchester United, Spurs, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

Leicester remain in discussions with Arsenal over the sale of 16-year-old Jeremy Monga. The Foxes also want a sell-on clause included.

Abdul Fatawu celebrates Ghana's win over Panama at the World Cup last week

Wrexham legend Mullin to leave this summer

Wrexham striker Paul Mullin will leave the club this summer following the mutual termination of his contract.

Mullin, 31, played a huge role in Wrexham’s rise from the National League to the Championship with 110 goals in 172 appearances following his arrival from Cambridge United in 2021.

Newcastle add Nmecha to their shortlist

Newcastle have Germany's World Cup midfielder Felix Nmecha on their shortlist this summer. The 25-year-old has a £73.5m buyout at Dortmund but a deal could be negotiated at a lower price.

The Magpies face losing Sandro Tonali, who is wanted by Tottenham, while Arsenal have seen an approach for Bruno Guimaraes rebuffed.

Nmecha is one of several midfielders they are considering and a deal to get him out of Dortmund would be expensive. However, he is admired and has been on the club's and Eddie Howe's radar for several years.

Manchester United have also been linked, but he is not thought to be near the top of their shortlist.

Craig Hope

Felix Nmecha has started all three group games for Germany at this World Cup

Brentford looking at Burnley's Anthony

Brentford have added Burnley’s Jaidon Anthony to their list of transfer options.

The Bees are already keen on the winger’s Turf Moor team-mate Zian Flemming and they are exploring a move for Hoffenheim’s coveted Ivory Coast international flyer Bazoumana Toure too.

Spurs must give up 10 per cent of Bergvall cash

Djurgarden are due 10 per cent of any fee that Tottenham may receive for Lucas Bergvall. The Swedish midfielder is high on Nottingham Forest’s wishlist as they look to fill the void left by Elliot Anderson’s pending departure.

Spurs would want around £45m for the 20-year-old who is keen to find more regular playing time and fears options will be limited as Roberto de Zerbi pushes for Newcastle’s Sandro Tonali and West Ham’s Mateus Fernandes.

Lucas Bergvall in action for Sweden against Japan last night - both sides are into the last 32

Leicester defender eyed by Torino

Leicester City centre back Ben Nelson is attracting attention from Torino in Italy.

The 22-year-old, who can also play left back, has a number of clubs monitoring his situation. The former England U20 international has been on the radar of Manchester United previously and other Premier League sides.

Anderson set for City medical

Elliot Anderson will have his Manchester City medical in the coming days after the club agreed a deal with Nottingham Forest.

City sources insist the deal for the England midfielder, 23, is £116m (€135m), a club record, with no bonuses attached.

Read more on the move from Daily Mail Sport HERE

Newcastle dismissive of Arsenal move for Bruno

Newcastle are understood to be dismissive of Arsenal's approach for Bruno Guimaraes.

Daily Mail Sport last night revealed the club were braced for the Gunners to make a move, with representatives in the UK gauging the market for the Brazil international.

He has two months to run on his contract.

Sports.content:
Man City strike £116MILLION breakthrough for Elliot Anderson: England star set for medical in the United States while on World Cup duty as Nottingham Forest man nears mega-money move

H ave you paid attention to the action so far? Try our World Cup quiz HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City have agreed a deal worth £116million with Nottingham Forest to make Elliot Anderson the first signing of the post-Pep Guardiola era.

The England midfielder is currently in the United States at the World Cup and a medical will now be arranged – with the expectation that he becomes a City player over the coming days.

Anderson is nursing a slight glute concern ahead of England facing Panama on Saturday but it is not thought to be serious and no scan has been necessary.

City were believed to have agreed an initial £106million fee with Forest last week, with Daily Mail Sport revealing earlier this month that Evangelos Marinakis was looking to secure a British-record £130m after add-ons.

Negotiations between the two clubs over the past few days centred on the make up of add-ons and the timeframe in which they are paid down.

But after a breakthrough in talks, City sources now stress that the deal for Anderson is a straight one-off payment and are playing down the idea that they have eclipsed the £125m that Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak.

Elliot Anderson is on the verge of joining Manchester City after a fee was agreed with Nottingham Forest

Anderson will, however, become the most expensive English footballer of all time ahead of Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham. The 23-year-old has made it clear that City was his preferred destination, with personal terms already agreed.

England boss Thomas Tuchel has already said he would facilitate summer transfers of players in his squad, and arrangements for Anderson will now be made. Personal terms will not be an issue.

Anderson’s focus is England and the World Cup and those involved are relaxed about the timings around the completion of the move.

There is no sell-on clause for Newcastle, who sold Anderson to Forest for £35m in 2024 as they scrambled to avoid breaching PSR rules.

Sports.title: Why Noni Madueke is one of Thomas Tuchel's favourites: England insiders reveal the dressing down that put 'frustrating' youngster on right path, unseen qualities that set him apart and why 'goldfish memory' is winger's secret weapon
Sports.content:
Why Noni Madueke is one of Thomas Tuchel's favourites: England insiders reveal the dressing down that put 'frustrating' youngster on right path, unseen qualities that set him apart and why 'goldfish memory' is winger's secret weapon

Unlock more from our team inside the England camp at the World Cup with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and analysis

Seven hundred and ninety-two people were at Alfreton Town when an England side boasting Cole Palmer, James Trafford and Tino Livramento beat South Korea by two unanswered goals scored before half-time almost seven years ago.

Palmer scored one of them. And the other came from a youngster who was dealing with persistent question marks then, and still does to this day.

Noni Madueke pinched the second for an Under 18s team that has since produced several senior internationals. Morgan Rogers was around it at the time too, having completed a seven-figure move to Manchester City weeks earlier.

The FA had a frightening amount of talent at their disposal and the jostling for positions – in that squad but also to remain visible when leaving academy football behind – was on.

In terms of ability, little could separate many of them. The fine margins, the one per cent, would mark who went on to record true international honours.

With Madueke, a 17-year-old who had turned down Manchester United when leaving Tottenham for PSV Eindhoven in search of first-team football, there were key areas for improvement. FA coaches set about moulding him into somebody whose attributes eventually caught the eye while under Lee Carsley and have earned the trust of Thomas Tuchel, starting both games at this World Cup so far.

Noni Madueke has become a shoo-in for England, having earned the trust of boss Thomas Tuchel

Madueke was England’s most dangerous attacker against Ghana before losing his way in the second half

His rise with England didn’t start at Alfreton, during that September 2019 camp of three friendlies, but is certainly defined by it.

‘Noni showed glimpses of being a player who has the technical ability and tactical understanding,’ says Ian Foster, the coach then trusted with bringing youngsters through the pathway. ‘But there were parts I found particularly frustrating – defensive work and his attitude towards that.’

Foster, who went to Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ettifaq as Steven Gerrard’s assistant in 2023, gathered some coaches and analysts together to give a presentation to him.

They used Gareth Southgate’s seniors as a benchmark, looking over data and clips from victories over Bulgaria and Kosovo. Raheem Sterling and Marcus Rashford were the wingers. Madueke sat and watched that through with Foster on arrival for international duty in October. It delivered a message.

‘We reminded him that talent wasn’t enough,’ Foster adds. ‘Look at who else is trying to get in the team: you need to offer more than ability. Talented wingers can show you that they can do the dirty work and choose when to do it. What we demonstrated to him is that you can’t do that at the top level. He said, “Right, watch me”.

‘His performances after that were outstanding. He scored an unbelievable goal in Poland a month after and he actually captained the team in November based on his behaviours off the pitch. The penny dropped.’

This is perhaps instructive of why Madueke is here ahead of Palmer or Phil Foden. Through the Under 21s, when winning the European Championship three years ago, to now under Tuchel, he has been seen as reliable.

He is undoubtedly an FA project and shaped in a way that means he can contribute on the biggest stage. Follows instructions, mucks in. Those who know him insist that the final piece, the final ball, will come.

Madueke came through the FA pathway, winning the Under-21 Euros in 2023

Madueke's relentless repetitions of practising off both feet accelerated his progression and made him a trickier winger to deal with

Doubts have surrounded him throughout his career. Spurs didn’t appear to put up much of a fight when PSV came calling. Going to Chelsea was a slow burn and then there was outcry when Arsenal spent £50million on him last summer, supporters even organising a petition against his signing.

But talking to others who know the 24-year-old, who has been holding up England’s right-hand side as Bukayo Saka deals with fitness problems, it has become clear why a spot on the plane never really appeared in doubt.

Sources say his ability to cope with extra attention has been a major plus, a similar attitude to Anthony Gordon over the years. His relentless repetitions of practising off both feet accelerated his progression and made him a trickier winger, happy to go inside or outside when met with a marker.

There were a few moments of this early on against Ghana when feeding Reece James or heading for the byline. Madueke went on to lose his way in the second half, mirroring everybody else before the late substitutions, but had been England’s most dangerous attacker.

He’s been described by staff as having a ‘goldfish memory’ – a capability of immediately shrugging off a mistake and ‘going again’ – and in major tournaments, when criticism flies, that is no bad trait to have.

There has been talk about finishers in this competition and how they will be the individuals to impact how far England go. While managing the fitness of Saka – his problem believed to be two-pronged and not only localised to the achilles – Madueke has been tasked with stretching defences for the majority and then letting his Arsenal team-mate do the rest.

Saka has labelled their situation, close friends battling for the same spot for club and country, as ‘unique’, which is definitely one word for it. ‘I don't really know how it works, but it does,’ Saka said of their relationship.

‘Noni speaks well, speaks honestly,’ Foster says. ‘I’d always try to create challenging conversations which will set them up. He’ll be brave in those meetings. You’ll challenge them tactically but to speak freely and handle those types of challenges is different. You can see the effect he has on his team-mates.

Madueke gives off the same vibe whether he starts, comes off the bench or is not used at all

Bukayo Saka has labelled their situation, close friends battling for the same spot for club and country, as ‘unique’. ‘I don't know how it works, but it does,’ Saka said of their relationship

‘When you’re going away for five weeks, living in each other’s pockets, it can be stressful. Some haven’t been selected in the past because of that. His attitude and behaviours will not change if he starts or finishes or isn’t involved.’

That was a key factor in the Under-21 tournament in Georgia, when Madueke lost his place for the semi-final and subsequently the final win over Spain. Emile Smith Rowe was preferred yet those present in the dressing room didn’t detect any change in Madueke’s demeanour. Against Spain, he bounded on from the substitutes' bench and put in a huge defensive effort as England remarkably ended the tournament without conceding a goal.

At the FA now, they discuss his brave decision to head for the Netherlands at 17. Ruud van Nistelrooy was Madueke's coach for the B team and kept in close contact with England to make sure both sides were on board with the development plan. It cannot be a coincidence that six weeks after that meeting on the donkey work, Madueke was named on the PSV first-team bench and soon made a senior debut. He ended up being unplayable, which is why Chelsea ultimately paid more than £28m for him.

‘I bumped into Ruud recently,’ Foster adds. ‘We were laughing. Noni’s such a character, a great kid. He brightens up a room when he comes in. Glass half full. You can have honest conversations with him.

‘If you give him an inch, he might just take a little bit more. But he’s not malicious in any sense. PSV were seeing the same thing as we were. You see them breaking their neck to score but can they do it the other way? He’s certainly learnt.

‘He’s kicked on again. There are question marks around his place but I don’t see that. I had him for three years and know how special he can be.’

Sports.title: 'Anyone who understands football values him enormously': Meet Spain's unsung 'MVP' goal machine Mikel Oyarzabal - and why Tottenham or Man United should hijack Barcelona move for the man outshining Lamine Yamal
Sports.content:
'Anyone who understands football values him enormously': Meet Spain's unsung 'MVP' goal machine Mikel Oyarzabal - and why Tottenham or Man United should hijack Barcelona move for the man outshining Lamine Yamal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mikel Oyarzabal has done everything in his power to buck the trend of the egotistic centre forward.

He doesn’t have a super agent in his corner – he leaves all that to mum Dorleta and dad Ernesto – and he’s never generated a transfer fee, spending his entire career to date at Real Sociedad. Not one to chase social media clout, Oyarzabal has just 359,000 Instagram followers. By contrast, Spain’s third-choice goalkeeper Joan Garcia has 3.1 million.

He is not extravagant in his fashion choices – one Spanish broadcaster described him as ‘styling his hair like a kid from a private school’ – nor all that fussed if every one of his team-mates takes the limelight away from him.

Oyarzabal, 29, happily swaps red carpet appearances and parties for spending time with his partner Ainhoa, who is a doctor, and their young son. But what that has done is create a misconception that Oyarzabal isn’t one of the world’s best strikers. That he is. Just ask any player, past or present.

‘I’m confused by modern football,’ Zlatan Ibrahimovic said on FOX after Spain’s 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia. ‘I watched Spain today and when the game finished, all I saw was people talking about Lamine Yamal. Did we even watch the same game?

‘For me, Mikel Oyarzabal was the one doing the dirty work. If Oyarzabal played the exact same game with Lamine’s name on the back of his shirt, people would be calling it a Ballon d’Or-worthy performance right now. That’s the truth no one wants to admit.’

Spain's Mikel Oyarzabal, who goes quietly about his business, was superb in his side's 4-0 win over Saudia Arabia

Oyarzabal, in the right place at the right time, tucks home his second goal against Saudi Arabia

The truth is, Oyarzabal has always been like this. Unassuming in his manner, selective with his words, a leader without being bombastic, and desperate not to receive any special treatment.

It was why, while living in a four-bedroom student flat after making his first-team debut for Real Sociedad as an 18-year-old, he found himself locked out after returning home from a Copa del Rey match at 4am. With his flatmates asleep, rather than wake them up, he abandoned hopes of getting back to his bed.

It was also why when it came to assignments for his business administration degree at the University of Deusto, there was to be no special treatment compared to his classmates. Studying en route to away days and while team-mates played video games, Oyarzabal was happy to just blend in.

At 18, Lionel Messi was scoring at the 2006 World Cup. At that same age, Yamal had already scored at a World Cup. Cristiano Ronaldo was a Manchester United regular, lighting up the Champions League.

When Oyarzabal was 18, his head was buried in his books. He wouldn’t even grace the world’s biggest tournament until he was 29, robbed of a spot at the 2022 World Cup due to a cruciate ligament injury that sidelined him for nine months.

So no, there isn’t the hype, appreciation, the razzmatazz that follows strikers like a shadow, with Oyarzabal. But there should be. Few players are as revered and celebrated by fellow pros as the Spaniard, making it all the more remarkable how so few fans see him in the same light.

Oyarzabal is under contract with Real Sociedad until 2028 with a release clause of €75million (£64m), although Barcelona, who have him as their back-up plan to Julian Alvarez, are targeting a fee closer to £30m.

And in a market where Premier League clubs are paying north of £85m for strikers, Aston Villa, Everton, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur, all of whom would benefit immensely from a new forward like Oyarzabal, would be mad not to look at him. Man City and Arsenal have liked him in the past, though at 29 that window might have passed.

Oyarzabal scores Spain's second goal, his first, against the Saudis. 'Anyone who understands football values him enormously,’ Spain boss Luis de la Fuente said this week

Publicly and privately, Spain's wonderkid Lamine Yamal is in awe of his team-mate, often referring to him as the nation’s MVP (Most Valuable Player)

‘Anyone who understands football values him enormously,’ Spain boss Luis de la Fuente said this week. ‘For some people, the impact he has may seem small, but here we know just how significant it is.’

Publicly and privately, Yamal is in awe of his team-mate, often referring to him as the nation’s MVP (Most Valuable Player). Marc Cucurella said of Oyarzabal recently: ‘Perhaps not many people thought Mikel had that level before. But I always said that when you play with him, you realise what he brings.’

But you should not need to play with Oyarzabal to know his immense quality. This is a player who is joint-seventh on Spain’s all-time goalscoring charts alongside Fernando Morientes. This is a player who has scored in all six of the major finals he has played in, including scoring the winning goal against England to clinch the 2024 European Championship.

This is a player who has scored in seven of Spain’s last eight games. This is a player who everyone inside that Spain dressing room looks to for leadership.

‘You can lead and set an example without going crazy, without shouting, without being a disciplinarian,’ Oyarzabal said on the eve of the World Cup. ‘There are several ways, and they are all equally valid.’

That’s not to say he hasn’t got a sharp tongue when it’s required, though. ‘Mikel is like a mother,’ team-mate Nico Williams explained. ‘He scolds you when necessary and shows you affection when you need it.’

But being unfashionable and unassuming means the good and the bad can often get overlooked. In Spain's shock 0-0 draw against Cape Verde, Oyarzabal became the first player on record since 1966 to go the first 30 minutes of a World Cup match with exactly zero touches. Few outside of Spain picked up on it.

Next up, against Saudi Arabia, an unplayable Oyarzabal scored twice and added an assist inside 24 minutes, becoming just the third player since 1966 to record three goal involvements in the opening half-hour of a World Cup game. Again, many were too preoccupied with the ‘bigger’ name forwards to pay much attention to him.

Oyarzabal, who has never commanded a transfer fee, is under contract with Real Sociedad until 2028 and has a release clause of £64m

In the early hours of Saturday morning, Spain play their final group match against Uruguay. Don't bet against Oyarzabal scoring again.

‘The funny thing about Oyarzabal is that people keep talking about other stars, and he just keeps producing numbers that most strikers would only dream of,’ said Paul Scholes after the Saudi Arabia game.

‘Fourteen goals and seven assists in 13 games (Oyarzabal's recent record for Spain) is ridiculous. If a bigger-name player were achieving those numbers, we'd be hearing about it every day.’

At some point soon, Oyarzabal will shed the ‘underrated’ tag he loathes for good. And then talk will go from people doubting him to asking themselves: how on earth did we not appreciate him sooner?

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe vs Erling Haaland: The France star is the hungriest and the best he has looked for some time while Norway's focal point is a ruthless goal-poacher supreme... but who will come out on top tonight?
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe vs Erling Haaland: The France star is the hungriest and the best he has looked for some time while Norway's focal point is a ruthless goal-poacher supreme... but who will come out on top tonight?

Have you paid attention to the action so far? Try our World Cup quiz HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

I watched Scotland’s defeat by Brazil on Wednesday evening in a bar in rural New Hampshire. One of the other customers saw me staring up at the screen and wanted to know all about the France-Norway game at Boston Stadium, home of his beloved New England Patriots, tonight.

‘Who’s that amazing guy that plays for France?’ he asked, apologising for his lack of knowledge. I told him that could mean one of quite a few players but that he was probably thinking of Kylian Mbappe. ‘That’s the one,’ he said. ‘He’s the boss hog.’

It is the first time I have heard Mbappe called that but maybe it’s not the worst description. I was in Philadelphia on Monday evening to see France dismantle Iraq and Mbappe was so sharp and eager, so demanding and ambitious that his performance was breathtaking.

And tonight, for the first time at this World Cup, one of the great Alphas of the tournament will come up against another one: Mbappe’s is likely to line up against Erling Haaland in a struggle between two of the world’s great goalscorers.

Mbappe is only 27 but he is already a veteran of two World Cup finals. He won the first and scored a hat-trick in the second. The four goals he has scored already in this tournament have taken him to 16 in World Cups in 16 games. Only Lionel Messi — who has 18 — has scored more.

Haaland is playing in his first World Cup but he is established in club football as a goalscoring machine. He has 112 goals in 132 Premier League appearances for Manchester City and, to no one’s great surprise, has hit the ground running in his tournament debut here.

Kylian Mbappe could line up against Erling Haaland tonight in a battle of two of the world's great goalscorers

Mbappe's four goals at this tournament have taken him to 16 in total at the World Cup, with only Lionel Messi having scored more

Haaland is level with Mbappe in the golden boot race after scoring twice in both his of Norway's matches at his first World Cup

He has scored in every competitive game he has played for Norway going back to October 2024, which makes 24 goals in 12 competitive games. He scored twice in Norway’s first game of the tournament against Iraq and twice more against Senegal.

Which means that Mbappe and Haaland are tied on four goals each, one behind Messi, in a race for the Golden Boot that is shaping up to be the most compelling for decades. Vinicius Junior, Harry Kane and Cristiano Ronaldo are massing behind them.

Should both Mbappe and Haaland start in a game that pits two sides who have already qualified for the last 32 against each other, it will provide an enthralling clash of styles and attributes.

There is a suggestion that Norway will rotate heavily tonight but that Haaland will start the game if he wishes to. The most likely scenario is thought to be that he will play for an hour or so and then be substituted. The same may apply to Mbappe.

Mbappe was like quicksilver against Iraq. After a difficult, uneven season with Real Madrid, this is the hungriest and the best he has looked for some time. His movement was a blur and his hunger for goals was insatiable.

His first goal that night was a stunning hit from outside the box that went through a defender’s legs and rocketed past the keeper. His second was a tap-in after an unselfish lay-back from Ousmane Dembele.

Mbappe can score from anywhere and he can create goals from nothing with his frightening pace and mesmeric control.

He also has a quite brilliant supporting cast. When the Ballon d’Or winner is teeing up tap-ins for you, you know the cards are stacked in your favour.

Mbappe has looked the hungriest and best he has for some time in France's opening matches

The France captain is backed by a quite brilliant supporting cast that includes Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele

Haaland is a better finisher than Mbappe but does not possess the all-round game of the Frenchman

Haaland is more reliant on support, but does have the supreme creative talent of Martin Odegaard to help him

Haaland does not have the same level of support, although in Arsenal’s skipper, Martin Odegaard, he does have a sublime creative talent to work with who appears to be relishing the tournament after a long, hard Premier League title race against Haaland’s City.

Haaland is also more reliant on support. He is a goal-poacher supreme, one of the most clinical and ruthless finishers that English football has seen but the vast majority of his goals are from close range. He is a better finisher than Mbappe but he does not have the all-round game the France captain possesses.

Both represent their team’s best chance of winning tonight and both will be desperate to play. Topping Group I appears to offer a gentler route through the first couple of knockout rounds than qualifying as runner-up.

The winner could face a route of Sweden in the last 32, Germany in the last 16, the Netherlands in the quarter-finals, Spain in the semis and then the final. The runner-up could face Ivory Coast, Brazil, England, Argentina and then the final.

For those trying to predict the eventual winner of the Golden Boot, the strength of the respective sides offers the best clue. Coming into the tournament, France and Spain were generally regarded as the two strongest sides. As the tournament nears the end of the group stage, that perspective has not changed.

If France stay in the competition longer than Norway, as expected, then Mbappe has a better chance than Haaland of adding another Golden Boot to the one he won at Qatar 2022. It seems likely that the tally of eight goals, which he set there, will be surpassed this time.

‘I would have to side with Mbappe,’ Tony Cascarino, the former Republic of Ireland striker, wrote recently, ‘mainly because I fancy France’s chances to reach the final more than Argentina’s.

‘But also because Mbappe has proved that he can do it on the biggest stage, including a hat-trick in the final in Qatar four years ago. Regardless of who wins it, I would be shocked if the final tally does not reach eight goals,.’

Is Just Fontaine’s all-time record at a single tournament of 13, set in 1958, reachable? It is as hard to see that happening as it is to imagine that anyone will ever beat Dixie Dean’s record of 60 goals in an English top-flight season. Even Haaland’s best shot fell short at 36.

Sports.title: South Korea fans launch petition calling for manager to be axed after dropping captain Son Heung-min from starting line-up in South Africa defeat - as nation face anxious wait to see if they will stay in the World Cup
Sports.content:
South Korea fans launch petition calling for manager to be axed after dropping captain Son Heung-min from starting line-up in South Africa defeat - as nation face anxious wait to see if they will stay in the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

South Korea head coach Hong Myung-bo is facing calls to step down following the country's disastrous World Cup campaign, which saw them lose 1-0 to Group A weak-links South Africa.

It wasn't just the result, which leaves their World Cup campaign hanging in the balance, that had South Korean fans raising their fists - but the manner in which they lost, dominating the ball but failing to create any clear-cut chances in a game which was far from eye-catching.

Only a tame Oh Hyeon-gyu header and an early Lee Kang-in strike were among their rare chances, and a petition calling for Hong to be sacked called it 'lifeless' and 'one of the worst displays by a Korean team' in their World Cup history - which leaves them anxious to see results go in their favour to book one of the eight third-place spots to progress to the knockout rounds.

The most controversial moment actually arrived before the game, with captain Son Heung-min dropped from the starting line-up for the first ever time in the former Spurs midfielder's career.

Despite being unable to find the back of the net in South Korea's first match victory against Czech Republic, and then failing to record a shot in their defeat to Mexico in their second, dropping their talisman was always a gamble which would backfire disproportionately if it failed.

Given that South Korea only needed to avoid defeat against the Group A underdogs to guarantee second place in the table, this certainly appears to be the position that we now find ourselves in, with Hong facing widespread calls from the country's football fan base and media to step down.

The most controversial moment actually arrived before the game, with captain Son Heung-min dropped from the starting line-up for the first ever time in the former Spurs midfielder's career

A petition from fans in the wake of the defeat argued that Hong's appointment had been tainted by procedural flaws from the outset and that it was 'fundamentally illegitimate'

Such has been the backlash that, in the post-match press conference, journalists described the South Korean performance as 'dismal'; another suggested that the only explanation for such a poor display was a case of 'mass food poisoning within the squad', and Hong's decision-making was labelled a 'failure'.

A petition from fans in the wake of the defeat argued that Hong's appointment had been tainted by procedural flaws from the outset.

It read: 'The Korea Football Association's official selection process was effectively ignored, making it difficult to avoid criticism that the appointment was fundamentally illegitimate.'

It continued: 'Despite fielding what many considered the strongest squad in Korea's World Cup history, the team finished with one win and two losses, placing third in the group.

'The performance against South Africa was so lifeless that it could be regarded as one of the worst displays by a Korean team in World Cup history.'

Aside from Hong's removal, the petition also urged sweeping reforms to the governance of the Korea Football Association (KFA).

Hong himself, who many believe would not have stayed beyond the end of this campaign, accepted 'full responsibility' in the wake of the defeat - and will therefore likely go quietly if asked to do so.

'In terms of the process and preparing for this game, and how we would play on the field, that is something I put much thought into,' said the former South Korea captain, who led the team to its famous semifinal finish in 2002 during his playing days. 'Of course, if we knew what the result was going to be, I probably would have made different choices.

'But I had a strategy in mind. Whenever such a bad result happens, everyone has their own opinion. The result is really the responsibility of the head coach. Ultimately, it comes down to my hands.

'I guess I made the wrong decisions and that was the reason we had a bad result. Nothing more, nothing less.'

As for his decision-making behind the exclusion of Son, Hong argued that he believed in the build-up to the match that the 33-year-old would be most ruthless when deployed against a tiring South African side - although he actually brought him on at the start of the second half, right after both teams had benefited from a break, and he had little impact on the game.

'We thought that Son would be better placed (to make an impact) when the opponents were losing their energy, not when they had a lot of energy,' Hong added. 'And when there were more spaces to exploit between the opponents' defensive line, that's when we wanted Son to be at his strongest - when the opponents were a bit weaker.'

South Korea could still squeeze into the Round of 32 given they currently sit sixth in the standings. As it stands, they will face Mo Salah's Egypt side next.

Even so, the country's football media are predicting that regardless of the outcome of the third-place standings, Hong's fate could already be sealed.

Sports.title: Oleksandr Usyk confirms he has vacated title belts with statement on retirement
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk confirms he has vacated title belts with statement on retirement

World heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk has confirmed he is going to vacate his title belts in a statement which gave a huge hint on his boxing future

View Image Oleksandr Usyk

Oleksandr Usyk has confirmed that he will vacate all his belts - but is not retiring from boxing.

‌



Fresh off the back of last month's controversial stoppage win against Rico Verhoeven, the 39-year-old has chosen to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has blown the heavyweight division wide open.

‌



However, Usyk won't be retiring from the sport just yet as he announced he will fight one last time before hanging up the gloves, though his next opponent has not been revealed.

‌



In a video on social media, the Ukrainian, who has an undefeated professional record of 25 wins from his heavyweight career, said: "It's a good day to say that I want to vacate all the belts I currently hold. I want to make them available so the guys who are next in line can fight for them.

"I'm leaving the belts but I'm not leaving the sport because I still have my last dance."

He added: "I want to thank everyone. I have great respect for all organisations. I want to thank everyone and say more to come."

‌



Usyk then wrote a separate post on X: "Attention [two exclamation mark emojis]. Important update... I am vacating my unified WBA, IBF and WBC heavyweight world titles ahead of stepping into the ring for my final fight."

"This is a well-considered decision that I am confident will open new opportunities for me. This is not the end of the story. The continuation lies ahead," he added in another post on X.

Usyk has been a champion in the heavyweight division since he knocked Anthony Joshua off his throne in 2021. He held the undisputed heavyweight title twice and and is also a former undisputed cruiserweight champion.

‌



The Simferopol-born boxer was due to fight challenger Agit Kabayel to keep the WBC title but it now appears the German will be promoted as the new champion by default.

Meanwhile, Moses Itauma is on course to fight for a heavyweight world title, with the young Brit scheduled to fight Croatia's Filip Hrgovic on August 29 at the O2 Arena in London.

The WBO title is held by Daniel Dubois and Itauma is expected to meet the Londoner in an all-British heavyweight bout in 2027.

Sports.title: Chelmsford City racecourse remains closed as licence appeal dismissed
Sports.content:
Chelmsford City racecourse remains closed as licence appeal dismissed

The Essex track lost an appeal against the BHA decision not to grant an operating licence to new company Golden Mile Racing Limited

View 2 Images Chelmsford City Racecourse remains shut

The future of racing at Chelmsford remains in doubt after an appeal by the racecourse’s intended new operating company against the decision of the British Horseracing Authority not to grant it a licence was dismissed.

‌



It was announced in April that three fixtures at Chelmsford, including the Essex track’s Good Friday fixture, had been cancelled after the BHA refused to grant a licence to Golden Mile Racing Limited. The new company was formed after the previous licence holder, Great Leighs Estates Limited, was placed in administration.

‌



A spokesperson for the BHA said on Friday: “We acknowledge the decision announced by the Licensing Committee today to dismiss the appeal by Golden Mile Racing Limited against the BHA’s decision to refuse it a licence to operate Chelmsford City Racecourse.

‌



“We note the committee’s finding that it was the applicant’s responsibility to satisfy the committee that a licence should be granted and that the material provided, including late and insufficiently detailed evidence, failed to do that.

England World Cup captain’s daughter debuts as racehorse trainer with first runner READ MORE :

“We also acknowledge the committee’s finding that the BHA executive and board had been ‘misled as to the likelihood of an administration by John Holmes and that Great Leighs Estates Limited (GLEL) had not been frank about its indebtedness’. “

‌



Chelmsford City Racecourse’s 12 racecourse fixtures remain with GLEL’s administrator and may be sold or transferred to a licensed racecourse operator, with the consent of the BHA.

View 2 Images Racing at Chelmsford is cancelled with track operator in administration (Image: Getty Images)

“The BHA’s racing department will continue to work with the National Trainers Federation, trainers, owners and other stakeholders to provide sufficient opportunities for horses within the race programme.

Article continues below

“With due regard to the committee’s decision-making process, we will carefully consider the full written reasons when they are published in due course before making a more substantive comment."

Sports.title: Christophe Soumillon: ‘I absolutely did not ride to benefit’ Aidan O’Brien runner at Ascot
Sports.content:
Christophe Soumillon: ‘I absolutely did not ride to benefit’ Aidan O’Brien runner at Ascot

The ten-time French champion jockey told a BHA independent judicial panel appeal that he was not involved in tactics designed to help a stablemate in the St James’s Palace Stakes

View 3 Images Christophe Soumillon has appealed against an 8 day ban (Image: PA)

Christophe Soumillon insisted on Friday he did not engage in tactics designed to benefit a stablemate of his Aidan O’Brien-trained mount at Royal Ascot.

‌



The ten-time French champion jockey was banned for eight days for his riding of Puerto Rico, the stable second string to Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Gstaad, in the £700,000 St James’s Palace Stakes.

‌



The race was billed as a rematch between Gstaad and Bow Echo, who had defeated the Ballydoyle challenger in the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket earlier this year. Puerto Rico, a Group 1-winning two-year-old under Soumillon last year, was the 16-1 outsider who took up the running early in the race.

‌



Soumillon took at least two glances behind him, including when entering the straight when Puerto Rico moved to the left, as a result of which a golden highway on his inside along the rail opened for Ryan Moore to make his challenge on Gstaad.

England World Cup captain’s daughter debuts as racehorse trainer with first runner READ MORE :

Moore took up the invitation but the staying-on Gstaad could not quite reel in Bow Echo, failing by a short head. Puerto Rico finished last of the six runners.

At a stewards inquiry Soumillon was found guilty of riding Puerto Rico “in such a way that intended to give an advantage to another horse from the same stable, in that he moved his mount away from the rail thereby ensuring a clear run for Gstaad on his inside”.

‌



At an appeal hearing on Friday the panel was shown multiple angles of the race, including drone footage.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Louis Weston, representing the BHA, said: “What the video showed is what Mr Soumillon was doing. He intended to open up the space for Gstaad, his stablemate. Mr Soumillon is checking around him to see the position of his stablemate and if I am wrong in saying that that is the purpose of it, the effect of looking around in the way that he did was to see where Gstaad was.

‌



“He would have seen him and he would have seen that Gstaad was not in an advantageous position and his manoeuvre follows the view. He checks to see where Gstaad is. He then either manoeuvres Puerto Rico or fails to check Puerto Rico so that the horse goes wide.”

Soumillon, described by Weston as one of the greatest riders of his generation, gave lengthy evidence defending his actions.

He said O’Brien had not told him to ride for the benefit of another of his runners. “I never had any special asking from himself doing anything to help another horse from his stable anytime,” he said.

‌



View 3 Images Gstaad (left) was able to challenge along the far rail after Puerto Rico (obscured) was switched left early in the straight (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Soumillon explained that after walking the course, he took the view that the ground was slower close to the far rail.

During the race there was a lot of contact between Puerto Rico and Power Blue, who he alleged was being aggressively ridden by David Egan on his outside.

‌



The reason he had turned around during the race, he said, was because he had heard Talk Of New York clipping heels, which caused Puerto Rico to over-race.

“Something you always do naturally, you look what is going on behind if you hear clipping heels and also, because he was trying to push me in, I just wanted to make sure there was nothing going wrong on my inside," he said.

View 3 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

‌



On the second occasion he said he had again heard some clipping heels.

“Turning your head around means two things," he said. "You want to make sure there is safety for everyone because Mr Egan was trying to bring me in at that point as well and I didn’t want to go in and I wanted to make sure nobody was trying to come on my inside.”

He added: “I really don’t care at that time where Ryan Moore was and if he was inside or not.”

Article continues below

During cross-examination Weston said: “What’s happened here Mr Soumillon is, having checked on Gstaad twice, having seen Gstaad boxed in, you move away from the rail, across Mr Egan’s line, he can’t hold his line, you create space deliberately with the intent of delivering up space for Gstaad. Do you agree with me?”

“No I disagree because Mr Moore has other options he can take, he can come out,” Soumillon said.

The hearing was adjourned until Thursday.

Sports.title: F1 news: George Russell sends Lewis Hamilton message as Ferrari announce driver replacement
Sports.content:
F1 news: George Russell sends Lewis Hamilton message as Ferrari announce driver replacement

The Formula 1 Austrian Grand Prix takes place this weekend at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg

View 3 Images Lewis Hamilton has been praised by George Russell (Image: Mark Sutton - Formula 1, Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Sunday's Formula 1 Austrian Grand Prix promises yet another thrilling potential battle at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, with no fewer than four teams capable of fighting for the top step. Kimi Antonelli heads the drivers' standings by 41 points, although the Italian's DNF at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix handed Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari a golden chance to claw back 25 points, as the Briton claimed his maiden victory for the Scuderia.

‌



The 41-year-old has shown a marked improvement on his underwhelming first season with the Italian outfit, during which he failed to register a single podium. However, 2026 has given him the perfect platform to consign that to history, with four top-three finishes already to his name.

‌



While Mercedes and Ferrari are threatening to turn both title races into a two-horse contest with George Russell hot on their heels, defending champion Lando Norris is keeping pace with the frontrunners on 73 points, as are McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri on 68 and Max Verstappen on 55.

‌



With round eight now shaping up, Red Bull's home circuit could yet spring a few surprises at the sharp end of the grid. Here's a roundup of all the latest news and talking points ahead of Sunday's race in Austria.

Max Verstappen to lose another Red Bull ally to F1 rival as fresh blow emerges READ MORE :

Millions of F1 fans can watch Austrian Grand Prix for free as broadcaster makes huge move READ MORE :

Russell issues Hamilton title verdict

George Russell has cautioned that Mercedes face a serious challenge from Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari for the 2026 Formula 1 drivers' and constructors' titles. Russell, who has endured a difficult season and sits in third position, said: "It's great to see Lewis back doing what he does best."

"People were writing him off last year or even the year we were team-mates in '24. You know, 'Is he too old? Is he this? Is he that?' And then he goes and he's been smashing it for the last four or five races.

‌



"It just shows that you don't forget how to drive overnight. You need yourself, your team, the set-up, the understanding of the tyres, everything just to click. And when it clicks, you fly.

View 3 Images George Russell was complimentary about Lewis Hamilton (Image: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"That's where he is at the moment and for sure he is a big threat. Ferrari are a huge threat. Kimi is still very much the driver out front and is performing really incredibly and consistently. But Ferrari feel like they're coming and Lewis is at the forefront of that."

Hamilton, who secured his maiden victory for Ferrari at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix a fortnight ago, declined to dismiss a strong push heading into the latter half of the campaign: "I don't think it's impossible," he said.

The seven-time champion trails championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes by 41 points following his triumph in Spain, which demonstrated he had bounced back from a challenging debut season with Ferrari.

‌



F1 star replaced for Austrian GP session

Hamilton will face a different opponent in the opposing Ferrari garage this weekend as Charles Leclerc is set to be substituted by the Scuderia. While the seven-time world champion has been in excellent form, Leclerc has found it difficult to match his velocity in recent outings and even admitted he has copied Hamilton's car configuration in an attempt to close the gap.

Leclerc, 28, could reasonably benefit from additional practice time to adapt to his revised settings. Yet the team have opted to offer an opportunity to Dino Beganovic to take the wheel in FP1 instead - leaving Leclerc with 60 minutes less in the car than his team-mate.

Beganovic, who has been part of Ferrari's driver academy since 2020, is receiving a rare outing in the SF-26. The young Swedish racer has been engaged in development duties this season and was brought in at Barcelona a fortnight ago, assuming Hamilton's spot in FP1.

‌



View 3 Images Charles Leclerc was replaced for FP1 (Image: Clive Mason, Getty Images)

If there is a bright side for the Monegasque, it's that Hamilton appeared untroubled by the alteration and proceeded to claim victory in the race - something Leclerc hasn't achieved since the 2024 campaign. Leclerc will return to the cockpit for FP2 so that he can acquaint himself with the car and get up to pace as swiftly as possible.

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur is optimistic about a strong performance from his squad, saying: "We arrive in Austria encouraged by our positive showing over the past few races. We are fully aware that there is still a lot of work to do and that we must continue to focus on ourselves.

Article continues below

"We will approach this weekend with the same method and mindset that we have adopted since the start of the season. [We are] aiming to put together clean sessions in every respect, from track execution to the strategic decisions taken on the pit wall.

"We know that every weekend has a different story to tell, which is why we will continue to take the championship one race at a time."

Sports.title: Tymal Mills backing new state school cricket competition to break down 'barriers'
Sports.content:
Tymal Mills backing new state school cricket competition to break down 'barriers'

The former England seamer, 33, went to a state school in Suffolk and paid a special visit to the Sussex regional finals of the trailblazing new competition

View 3 Images Mills was speaking from the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup regional Sussex finals at Hove

Tymal Mills believes the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup is breaking down the ‘barriers’ he had to battle through to make it to the top.

‌



The former England seamer, 33, went to a state school in Suffolk and paid a special visit to the Sussex regional finals of the trailblazing new competition.

‌



The brainchild of Michael Vaughan, the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup is a national hard ball competition for state schools across the UK – with over 1,100 boys’ and girls’ teams from more than 800 schools entering the inaugural edition.

‌



Mills, who captains Sussex in the T20 Blast, was in attendance on a baking day at Hove as Brighton Aldridge Community Academy (BACA) triumphed over Midhurst Rother College (MRC) in the county finals.

View 3 Images (Image: Getty Images)

He hailed the initiative for broadening the demographic of students with a chance to play cricket and hopes more can enjoy the benefits of a sport that has given him so much.

‌



“It’s awesome and a brilliant day for the kids,” he said. “I was state school educated for my entire education and never found my way out to situations like this.

“There are a lot of barriers that state schools might naturally struggle for, so credit to all schools who have entered and all those who have made it this far.

“It’s a great initiative and a sign that things are starting to get a little bit better in terms of state school representation.

‌



“It’s about keeping the love of the game, enjoying away days and evenings after – cricket is such a sociable game like that.

“It’s a long and time-consuming game but it’s also very rewarding – it’s given me an awful lot.

“Hopefully these cricketers can get that experience and love for it – whether that’s going to be playing professionally or recreationally.”

‌



Devised by Vaughan and MCC chair Mark Nicholas, the tournament – named after state school-educated stars Ben Stokes and Heather Knight – is organised by the MCC Foundation and supported by Barclays and the Black Heart Foundation.

The boys’ and girls’ finals will be held on the Main Ground at Lord’s on September 10, with regional semi-finals taking place at Headingley and Wormsley in July.

View 3 Images Brighton Aldridge Community Academy (BACA) triumphed over Midhurst Rother College (MRC) in Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup regional Sussex finals

‌



The winners of each final will have their school names engraved on a new Honours Board inn the Writing Room of the Lord’s Pavilion and will raise a trophy made and designed by Thomas Lyte, the makers of the FA Cup.

The competition also sees schools in the independent sector assist with equipment and facilities, with many lending their grounds and pitches to those state schools who need it.

“It’s epic to play at Lord’s and that will be a dream come true,” he added. “The fact that potentially some kids here today can get the chance to do that is amazing.

Article continues below

“It’s amazing to see the support that’s been put behind the whole initiative. No matter what level or stage you want to see growth and things getting bigger year on year – 1,100 teams in year one is a great starting place and I’ve got no doubts all those teams will be back next year and more will join also.”

Over a thousand teams have

Sports.title: Alex Yee hails triathlon boom as thousands prepare for London T100
Sports.content:
Alex Yee hails triathlon boom as thousands prepare for London T100

Olympic champion Alex Yee says triathlon has transformed from a niche sport he was once reluctant to talk about into a mainstream movement inspiring thousands to take part.

View Image T100 Gold Coast 10km Run on 22nd March 2026 in Surfers Paradise, Queensland.

Alex Yee used to feel shy about ‘running around London in tiny shorts’ and never considered sharing his triathlon exploits.

‌



Now he documents his every move to more than 225,000 Instagram followers and, in July, will be joined on the capital’s streets by thousands of weekend warriors as part of the London T100 Triathlon event.

‌



Interest in triathlons and endurance running are enjoying a boom thanks in part to influencers such as Hugo Fry and Russ Cook, aka Hardest Geezer, who ran the length of Africa in 2024.

‌



Yee, who has starred in documentary-style series on his YouTube channel to showcase preparations for marathons in London and Valencia, has witnessed first-hand the effects of the sport’s surge in participation and believes it will keep moving forwards.

“I love it,” said Yee. “My school friends have started messaging me to say they’re doing triathlon for the first time, or that they've done their first triathlon. I guess they have an appreciation for what I do now! But they've also found it really self-fulfilling.

“For me, that's been really rewarding. Back in the day, triathlon was something I wasn't embarrassed to share, but it was something I never considered sharing. People didn't really understand.

‌



“Now, to see people taking part in running events or doing triathlons for the first time feels really nice. They're able to share in what I fell in love with.

“From something where I used to be a bit shy about wearing my tight shorts and running around the streets in London, to it now being celebrated, that's only a good thing. And it’s nice to have played a small part in inspiring people.”

Yee, who is set to make his first Diamond League appearance since 2019 when he takes part in the 5000m in Monaco next month, will soon be racing around his home city when the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) returns to the capital for the first time in 11 years.

‌



The event is part of the third London T100 Triathlon weekend on 25-26 July, with the T100 widely seen as triathlon’s version of the London Marathon. The world ’s best triathletes as well as 5,300 amateurs will take part in races of various distances over the weekend, with former England rugby union captain Chris Robshaw and Strictly Come Dancing pro dancer Julian Caillon among those signed up.

Yee has relished his recent London Marathon experiences, having set the second-fastest time ever by a Brit, behind only Sir Mo Farah, in 2025. This year, he acted as a pacer during a race which saw Sabastian Sawe win in a world record time of 1:59:30,

“It was very special to be part of a historic day,” said Yee. “It was a pretty surreal day to see those times come through. I had a blast doing it.”

‌



The WTCS London event, which offers qualification points for LA 2028, presents Yee with a unique opportunity to do something he never thought possible – return to his youth.

“I'm a London boy,” said Yee, who hails from Lewisham. “I grew up looking at the skyline that we'll be racing around.

“I look at lots of different moments in my career, like my successes, but being able to race in places that had such a defining impact on me – such as the London Olympics and other World Championship events held in London – means a lot.

Article continues below

“For me now, the next two years are all about trying to be the best person I can be in 2028 and hopefully deliver in Los Angeles.”

Watch British stars, including Alex Yee, Beth Potter and Georgia Taylor-Brown race the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London on Saturday 25 July, with Olympic qualifying points on the line. The elite women start at 1430 and elite men go at 1615, with live coverage on Triathlonlive.tv and TNT Sports in the UK.

Sports.title: Bizarre World Cup loophole leaves two nations both hoping to lose
Sports.content:
Bizarre World Cup loophole leaves two nations both hoping to lose

Austria and Algeria face off in their final World Cup 2026 group stage fixture in Kansas City on Sunday night, with both teams potentially benefiting from losing the game

View 3 Images Kansas City Stadium, also known commercially as Arrowhead Stadium, will host Austria vs Algeria

Austria and Algeria are poised to meet in their final World Cup 2026 group stage encounter on Sunday night, with neither side likely to be overly enthusiastic about the prospect of victory. FIFA's revamped format for the 2026 edition expanded the tournament from 32 teams to 48, increasing the number of groups from eight to 12.

‌



Consequently, finishing third no longer results in automatic elimination, and that removal of jeopardy has created a bizarre situation ahead of the knockout stages. This significant rule change means defeating a rival carries considerably more weight than simply racking up goals against weaker group opposition.

‌



There has been widespread criticism over FIFA's rule change and the potential threat it poses to the integrity of the competition. Not only have matches been labelled as 'dead rubbers', essentially meaning there is nothing at stake beyond pride, FIFA's rule amendment has actually meant that, for certain teams, it may be preferable to lose rather than to win in front of their travelling supporters.

‌



This could prove true for both Austria and Algeria, who go head-to-head in a Group J clash on Sunday. Rather than scrapping it out for victory as they did in their opening two matches, both nations might be better served by throwing the result and losing in Kansas City.

World Cup nation given bank holiday as next round qualification confirmed READ MORE :

Should Spain defeat Uruguay on Saturday morning, they will top Group H with seven points, having thrashed Saudi Arabia 4-0 in their previous outing and playing out a goalless draw with Cape Verde in their opening group fixture. This means the side finishing second in Group J would face the 2010 world champions.

With Argentina already confirmed as group winners and Jordan eliminated on the head-to-head rule, either Austria or Algeria will claim second or third place respectively. In essence, whichever side wins the match knows they will face Spain in the next round.

‌



It's a knockout tie many would expect Luis de la Fuente's men to navigate comfortably. And that is precisely why both Austria and Algeria might be tempted to lose the game.

View 3 Images Konrad Laimer's Austria face a conundrum at the World Cup (Image: Getty)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The situation has been branded the potential 'Disgrace of Kansas City' by football fans across social media, including Boston University economics professor Florian Ederer. "90 minutes of passive passing around at the back, 0-0 draw guarantees that both teams go through... and nobody wants to win because they have to play Spain in R32!" Ederer tweeted.

The reference harks back to the 'Disgrace of Gijon' 44 years ago, when Austria capitulated against West Germany in a 1-0 defeat at the 1982 World Cup during their final group match at El Molinón in Gijon. Ironically, it was Algeria who paid the price with an early exit as a direct result of Austria's defeat.

‌



It leaves both managers facing a peculiar situation in which neither side particularly wants to claim all three points. Even if Austria hold Algeria to a draw, it still does nothing to help them avoid Spain due to the goal difference rule, which comes into play when the head-to-head record is level.

In fact, a 1-0 defeat for Austria would likely represent their most favourable outcome. That would see them slip to third place while maintaining a decent enough goal difference to finish eighth or higher in the third-placed teams standings, securing their progression.

Austrian coach Ralf Rangnick has been open about his reluctance to be drawn against Spain in the Round of 32. Speaking to reporters this week, per Mundo Deportivo, the former Manchester United interim boss said Spain "is not an opponent anyone would want to face."

‌



View 3 Images Algeria face Austria at Kansas City Stadium with a dilemma (Image: Getty)

Algeria must tread carefully in pursuing such a strategy, however. Should they suffer a two-goal defeat, they would fall below Scotland in the third-place standings, leaving them dangerously close to the elimination zone, where Cape Verde, Belgium, DR Congo and Senegal currently find themselves.

Algeria coach Vladimir Petkovic conceded that his side have put themselves in a strong position, yet hinted they may not simply accept defeat. "I think ultimately we've produced two good performances. Ultimately to have our fate in our own hands. Nothing has yet been decided, but we're in a good position," he told reporters.

Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV

Our tipping ace has a big priced tip in the Pitmen's Derby, otherwise known as the Northumberland Plate, a major racing highlight in the north east

View 2 Images Steve Jones with his picks for Saturday

Stamina is the order of the day in the Pitmen’s Derby and SYNERGISM (3.15) could be the one to dig deepest in the Newcastle marathon.

‌



Officially called the Jenningsbet Northumberland Plate, it’s run over 2m on the all-weather and is a stiff test of staying power.

‌



Sir Mark Prescott’s runner fits the bill. He won twice over a few yards shy of today’s trip at Kempton last year and he only went down by half a length in a competitive Racing League handicap when attempting to complete the hat-trick. The form of that contest, run over today’s course and distance, worked out very well and he warmed up for a crack at this historic prize by winning at Lingfield on his first start of this season.

‌



England World Cup captain’s daughter debuts as racehorse trainer with first runner READ MORE :

He should be spot on for today. Have 1pt each-way at 14-1. A few bookies are paying out on six places.

The Jenningsbet Northumberland Vase – the consolation race for the main event – looks ideal for ST FAZ (2.40). He has an exceptional record on the all-weather. The only time he has been beaten on artificial surfaces was when badly hampered at the start in a hot Lingfield contest on Good Friday.

‌



He’s been running well on turf but he will love the return to the all-weather. Have 1pt each-way at 14-1. A couple of firms are offering six places.

View 2 Images Synergism ridden by Luke Morris (nearside, blue cap): Value Scope's fancy (Image: PA)

Earlier on the card, PABORUS (2.10) is interesting in the Group 3 Jenningsbet Chipchase Stakes. He hasn’t been seen on the track for exactly a year when he finished third in the Group 3 Criterion Stakes over 7f at York.
